_note: BASELINE (2026-08-18, before card-based matching): recall 0/5, precision 4/5. Two things that number records. (1) The design packet measured 1/5 recall using the alias layer; bumping CACHE_V from 3 to 4 during the hook-hardening work invalidated every cache entry, and rebuilt entries start with aliases: [] because `enrich` was never re-run. So the alias layer silently vanished and the one paraphrase that used to match (playwright) stopped matching: 1/5 -> 0/5 is our own regression, not a measurement artefact. It is not being fixed, because cards replace that representation entirely. (2) The packet claimed 5/5 precision measured on 3 prompts; with 5 silent cases, 'write a commit message for these changes' matches session 49269330 at exactly the threshold (score 6.0, hits commit+changes). The defended precision floor is therefore 4/5, not 5/5.

prompt: how do we pass a date range through the url to a screen
why: 1aedc9fe (39t, 'Add deeplink to model usage screen in Lovable') is URL/deeplink work -- a different area from the Playwright sessions that two other cases resolve to, so a pass here cannot come from one lucky session. Its card carries 'date-range', 'url-driven' and 'query-params' as topics and names the ts_from/ts_to range in the summary, while its TITLE shares nothing with the prompt: the match must come from the card body, and specifically from splitting hyphenated topic phrases into parts. Word-frequency topics never contained these terms, so before/after is a real signal.
